test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 22 Jan 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which battle laid the foundation of British colonialism in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Battle of Plassey**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The battle of Plassey**** **laid the foundation of** British colonialism in India**.
 
• The Battle of Plassey marked the beginning of nearly two centuries of British dominance in India for the** British East India Company**.
 
• It was a remarkably underwhelming military confrontation for an event of such historical significance, with the fall of the Nawab of Bengal owing largely to treason.
 
• The British East India Company, which had been granted a royal charter in 1600 to pursue trade in the East Indies, including the ability to organise its own army, represented Britain in India. A similar mission was assigned to the French East India Company.
 
• **Siraj ud-Daulah** took over as Nawab of Bengal in 1755 and embraced a pro-French attitude.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Second Anglo-Sikh War **was a military struggle in 1848 and 1849 between the Sikh Empire and the British East India Company.
 
• **The Battle of Buxar **took place on October 22, 1764, between the forces of the British East India Company, led by Hector Munro, and the combined armies of Mir Qasim, Nawab of Bengal until 1764; Shuja-ud-Daula, Nawab of Awadh; and Shah Alam II, Mughal Emperor.
 
• **The siege of Seringapatam, **which took place at the end of the Third Anglo-Mysore War in 1792, was a battle and siege of the Mysorean capital city of Seringapatam.
